newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SCA buys Italy's Cochis for 970 mln Skr.
newsitem.headline: SCA buys Italy's Cochis for 970 mln Skr.

text.p: Swedish forestry group SCA said on Wednesday it bought Italian packaging group Cochis for 970 million crowns, including debt.
The acquisition is expected to give synergies of 40-50 million crowns annually and will have a positive effect on SCA's earnings from day one, SCA said in a statement.

"The acqusition is part of SCA's western European strategy to increase its undertakings in southern Europe and to achieve an overall market share in corrugated board of about 15 percent," the company said.
"The Italian market is the second largest in Europe and is growing faster than other European markets."
Cochis, one of Italy's leading manufacturers of corrugated board, posted 1996 sales of about 650 million crowns and had a six percent market share in corrugated board boxes.
"As a result of the acquisition, SCA attains a market share in the corrugated board segment in Italy of about 14 percent and becomes the largest company in the sector," SCA said.
"The earnings trend is expected to continue to be favourable in 1997 and in line with 1996," the company said.
The purchase price corresponds to an earnings before income tax depreciation (EBITD) multiple of 4.5 on 1996 earnings.
The price is based on an agreement in principle reached in the autumn of 1996 and includes earnings for the first half of 1997, SCA said.
Cochis has four integrated corrugated board plants, three separate converting units and a small testliner mill, SCA said.
The Cochis family will keep managing the company, it said.
